title: Twins and Giants Face Off in Final Week of the Season
seoTitle: Twins and Giants Face Off in Final Week of Season
subtitle: Matchup between Minnesota and San Francisco marks the end of the campaign
excerpt: With the Twins 3 games off the division lead and the Giants fighting to improve their record, the final series brings predictions and performance analysis.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the final week of the regular season, the Minnesota Twins and San Francisco Giants meet at Oracle Park to decide the final steps of campaigns marked by ups and downs. The matchup takes center stage as the Twins are still fighting for division positioning, while the Giants look to improve their win-loss record.

Recent Performance of the Twins

After starting the season with a surprising run, the Twins reached 56-55 by the end of July, just three games out of the American League Central lead. Since then, the team went 17-28, closing the campaign with 73 wins and 83 losses.

The Twins' offense fell below league average (99 wRC+), and the defense ranked 25th in MLB at -38.4 runs. Injuries also loom large, with Byron Buxton sidelined due to a new injury. Taj Bradley emerged as a standout on the mound, offsetting the absence of Pablo López, but Joe Ryan's consistency seems to have waned.

Giants' Situation

The Giants close out the season with 64 wins and 92 losses, ranking 12th in wins over the last ten years. The team's defense finished at -34.5 runs, 23rd in the league. The latest rebuilding cycle brought two competitive seasons (2020 and 2021), but the team was unable to keep pace with competitors like the Padres and Diamondbacks.

In recent games, the team has maintained a slightly better performance on the road (36-39), but still lost 7 of the 9 head-to-head matchups against the Twins in this series.

Series Predictions

Projected starting pitchers for the series include Blade Tidwell (1-2, 4.56 ERA) against Zebby Matthews (9-10, 4.74 ERA) on Monday; Anthony Molina (3-1, 4.18 ERA) against Taj Bradley (11-6, 3.81 ERA) on Tuesday; and Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.72 ERA) against a pitcher yet to be announced on Wednesday.

Kody Clemens, with 26 home runs on the season, has the potential to reach the 30-mark, especially in road games. Jung Hoo Lee is six extra-base hits away from matching his total from the previous season (51), having already recorded 31 doubles both last year and this year.

Historical Context of the Matchups

Over the last ten years, the Twins accumulated 763 wins to 749 losses, while the Giants recorded 735 wins and 777 losses. This difference reflects periods of greater success for the Twins, who had five winning seasons and four playoff appearances in the last decade, compared to just one winning season and one playoff appearance for the Giants.

What the Series Could Mean

For the Twins, a win can bolster hopes of finishing the season closer to the division lead. For the Giants, improving their record could ease pressure on the coaching staff and offer a bright spot heading into the offseason.
